Why LoomiUI

Six reasons LoomiUI feels different from a typical component kit, each one shown with the same live components your app can import.

01 / Portability

Actually framework-agnostic

Every component is a real custom element built with Lit. Drop<loomi-button> into React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML, or a CMS template — no wrapper packages, no framework-specific build. It's the exact same tag, everywhere, because it's just a custom element.

Same markup, four homes
App.jsx
<loomi-button color="primary">Buy now</loomi-button>
App.vue
<loomi-button color="primary">Buy now</loomi-button>
App.svelte
<loomi-button color="primary">Buy now</loomi-button>
index.html
<loomi-button color="primary">Buy now</loomi-button>
Buy now
02 / Scoped styling

No Tailwind at runtime

Components are authored with Tailwind, but it's compiled away at build time and inlined into each component's Shadow DOM. Consumers never install Tailwind and never fight a global stylesheet — styles can't leak in or out.

Global payload check
Typical UI kit + Tailwind~38kb CSS
@loomi/button, installed alone0kb global CSS
Styled, scoped, shipped
03 / Brand control

Theme with one CSS variable

Override --loomi-primary-600 (or any of the 14 palette colors) from your page's own CSS and every component re-skins instantly — no rebuild, no config file. Try it on the right.

04 / Package shape

Install exactly what you need

npm install @loomi/button pulls in only the button and its direct dependencies. Want everything? npm install @loomi/componentsgets the whole library in one shot.

Install map
single componentnpm install @loomi/button lit
or
entire librarynpm install @loomi/components lit
1button package
12category bundles
44full suite
05 / Native behavior

Real form participation

Every form control is form-associated via ElementInternals — they submit with a native <form> like any built-in input, across the shadow boundary. Fill this in and submit it — the values on the right come straight from a real FormData.

Built for AI-assisted coding
